metadata.title: ACDM flavored fried chicken version of Galaxy Dynamics
metadata.description:
RESEARCH EXPERIMENT: the author does not believe the LCDM recipes, halos or particle readings here. It maps how a LCDM group could reverse-engineer the law, so the route is on record first; nothing here is a framework result. Working note, version 1.7 (2026-11-04). AI-assisted; not peer reviewed; not reproduced by any outside group. kappa = 1/2 is fitted; the theory is not closed; nothing here says the data favour this law over LCDM. Fried chicken is a nickname and carries no physics. An analytic stand-in for feedback, not a hydrodynamic simulation. New in 1.5: the title spelling is corrected (Dynamics), and Amendment A13 asks whether any scale already in LCDM supplies the dark energy tie with no hand term. None does. Milgrom's coincidence c^2 sqrt(Lambda/3)/2 pi matches the number (kappa_eff 0.461, flat in z) but Lambda's pull at 10 kpc is 1.1e-5 a0, so it acts on nothing in a galaxy; cH/2 pi rises 3.4 times by z 2.33; the NFW central acceleration is 0.83 a0 at 1e12 solar masses but spans about 0.5 dex either way over mass and scales wrongly with cosmology; the Tully-Fisher scale at the cosmic baryon fraction is 0.20 a0. New in 1.6: Amendment A14, LCDM plus one named ingredient. None ties the scale to dark energy: feedback through the stellar-to-halo mass relation gives 1.7 a0 at 1e12 solar masses but spreads 0.83 dex over mass and rises 3.2 times by z 2.33; a halo edge set by Lambda is only 0.001 a0 and grows as M^(1/3); coupled quintessence has no acceleration scale; a posited halo times Lambda product is 0.005 a0 and no LCDM term makes it. New in 1.7: a correction and Amendment A15. Version 1.6 understated the halo route, judging the NFW central acceleration over too wide a mass range. Per SPARC galaxy the halo scale is 0.61 a0 with 0.16 dex spread and rises 1.5 times by z 2.33, so it does not supply the dark energy tie; but with one global factor it ties the law on observed rotation curves (0.1941 dex against the law's 0.1951). On observable gates alone Milgrom's Lambda coincidence cannot be told from the tie; only a mechanism separates them. A self-interacting core with one cross-section fails at 0.12 dex.

How easily can LCDM's knobs reproduce the law g_N = g^2/(g + a0), on the measured baryons of 171 SPARC galaxies? Twelve supernova-feedback knobs, as one global recipe, land the fitted scale within 0.3 % of a0 and 0.0415 dex from the law (0.0445 on held-out galaxies), and score 0.1953 dex against observed curves, the law scoring 0.1951. Fourteen knobs reach 0.0275 dex. Six knobs per galaxy within 2 sigma priors pass the frozen 0.02 dex target at 0.0152 dex, with at least half the galaxies at the low concentration bound. The tie to dark energy did not come from the knobs: five hand-written terms at extreme values, and kappa still narrowly missed. Tuned to the law, so a match shows freedom, not explanation. All knobs disclosed; recipes added after first numbers are marked. New in 1.1: R12, a CDM halo defined from the formula with a = kappa c sqrt(G rho_DE), kappa = 1/2 by hand. It passes every target exactly by construction, which is not evidence, and the tie needs a coupling to dark energy that LCDM does not contain. Also new, a grade on KiDS-1000 lensing, 60 points, nothing refitted, gate p >= 0.01. All rows fail: law 276.1, twelve knobs 277.9, fourteen knobs 242.1, R12 stopped at R200 with a two-halo term 457.7, untuned LCDM control 563.1. New in 1.2: R13, one global recipe with 21 knobs and 5 hand terms, tuned jointly to the law on SPARC, to KiDS and to X-COP, against a frozen scoreboard. Verdict: not complete, failing the exact law target, KiDS (145.2 on 60 points), holdout and plausibility. R14 passes KiDS only with per-bin freedom, and every line passes only as a patchwork of about 1066 parameters, not one theory. On X-COP and KiDS the tuned recipe fits the data better than the plain law (mean -0.467 dex and 276.1). Also an effective particle reading, which the author does not hold as physics: no single equation of state holds these halos, and a real particle halo passes Cassini and predicts Newtonian wide binaries. New in 1.3: a one-scale action tying the field's cap to rho_DE, reproducing the law to 0.00004 dex. It is a posit, not a derivation; kappa stays fitted and it has no cosmology yet. Prior art is cited: the field equation is Zhao and Famaey 2006, and a limited search found close neighbours but no exact match. New in 1.4: this notice, and a correction: the capped function in the one-scale action comes from the author's own earlier AeST embedding, PAPER59 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23585319), which v1.3 failed to cite. New in 1.5: the title spelling is corrected (Dynamics), and Amendment A13 asks whether any scale already in LCDM supplies the dark energy tie with no hand term. None does. Milgrom's coincidence c^2 sqrt(Lambda/3)/2 pi matches the number (kappa_eff 0.461, flat in z) but Lambda's pull at 10 kpc is 1.1e-5 a0, so it acts on nothing in a galaxy; cH/2 pi rises 3.4 times by z 2.33; the NFW central acceleration is 0.83 a0 at 1e12 solar masses but spans about 0.5 dex either way over mass and scales wrongly with cosmology; the Tully-Fisher scale at the cosmic baryon fraction is 0.20 a0. New in 1.6: Amendment A14, LCDM plus one named ingredient. None ties the scale to dark energy: feedback through the stellar-to-halo mass relation gives 1.7 a0 at 1e12 solar masses but spreads 0.83 dex over mass and rises 3.2 times by z 2.33; a halo edge set by Lambda is only 0.001 a0 and grows as M^(1/3); coupled quintessence has no acceleration scale; a posited halo times Lambda product is 0.005 a0 and no LCDM term makes it. New in 1.7: a correction and Amendment A15. Version 1.6 understated the halo route, judging the NFW central acceleration over too wide a mass range. Per SPARC galaxy the halo scale is 0.61 a0 with 0.16 dex spread and rises 1.5 times by z 2.33, so it does not supply the dark energy tie; but with one global factor it ties the law on observed rotation curves (0.1941 dex against the law's 0.1951). On observable gates alone Milgrom's Lambda coincidence cannot be told from the tie; only a mechanism separates them. A self-interacting core with one cross-section fails at 0.12 dex. New in 1.8: Amendments A16 to A20 grade the other dark matter models. None reaches the law exactly as one recipe, and none ties a0 to rho_DE. The closest is 0.0252 dex with 15 knobs and halos 0.64 dex heavy; wave dark matter 0.092, hydro-calibrated responses 0.073 to 0.084, self-interacting dark matter 0.080 globally and 0.049 with 343 per-galaxy parameters (0.110 on unseen galaxies), warm dark matter 0.116 to 0.120. An interacting vacuum gives kappa near 0.5 but drifts with redshift. ACDM mocks with SPARC's errors match the scatter but fit a0 0.23 to 0.42 dex high. New in 1.9: Amendments A21 to A24 grade published hydrodynamic simulations, superfluid dark matter, dipolar dark matter and emergent gravity. No measured simulation scale reaches the law (best 0.029 dex) and none has been tested against varied Lambda. Superfluid dark matter misses by 0.037 to 0.081 dex and its tie to rho_DE needs a coupling set by hand. Dipolar dark matter reaches the law exactly only by choosing its free function to have the law's shape, with its link to Lambda imposed. Emergent gravity misses by 0.039 dex; its de Sitter reading gets kappa 0.48 and a flat a0(z), as the Lambda coincidence with 1/6, but not one constant across galaxies.
